nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Renewable energy usage preference_qna_000
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: Why is nuclear energy described as a cornerstone of the transformation in the energy landscape?
nodes.answer: Nuclear energy is considered a cornerstone because of its potential to provide reliable and clean energy, which is essential for meeting the growing global energy needs sustainably and responsibly.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Renewable energy usage preference_qna_001
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: Why is nuclear energy considered an attractive option for the future energy portfolio?
nodes.answer: Nuclear energy is attractive because it is a power-dense, carbon-free, and virtually emission-free energy source capable of large-scale energy production.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Renewable energy usage preference_qna_002
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: Why is the demand for renewable and sustainable energy sources increasing?
nodes.answer: The demand is increasing due to pressing issues of climate change, global warming, and the depletion of fossil fuel resources.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Renewable energy usage preference_qna_003
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How do companies view the use of renewable energy in relation to costs according to the survey results?
nodes.answer: The survey found that opinions were divided, with 32.2% abstaining, 20% disagreeing, and 20% agreeing on the potential increase in costs associated with renewable energy, reflecting the perceived barrier to its usage.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Renewable energy usage preference_qna_004
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What is the impact of environmental concern on the intention to pay more for renewable energy in developing countries?
nodes.answer: Environmental concern can positively influence the intention to pay more for renewable energy in developing countries, as individuals prioritize sustainability and environmental protection in their purchasing decisions.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Renewable energy usage preference_qna_005
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Which renewable energy resources show the highest growth in penetration?
nodes.answer: Wind and solar energy witness the highest growth in penetration among all renewable resources, while hydropower preference is on the decline in the scenarios.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Renewable energy usage preference_qna_006
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What sector is observed to have the highest renewable energy consumption among the four energy-consuming sectors?
nodes.answer: The residential sector is observed to possess the highest renewable energy consumption among the four energy-consuming sectors in all scenarios.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Renewable energy usage preference_qna_007
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: In the context of increasing energy preference, which renewable energy source has seen remarkable growth in the residential sector? How does the dominance of bioenergy in Latvia make it unique compared to other countries?
nodes.answer: Solar energy has experienced astonishing growth in the residential sector. In Latvia, bioenergy has dominated progress in the past 10 years, setting it apart from other countries in terms of renewable energy preference.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Renewable energy usage preference_qna_008
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why does Scenario 1 have the least fossil fuel increment value and the lowest renewable penetration?
nodes.answer: Scenario 1 has the least fossil fuel increment value and lowest renewable penetration because of the stagnant energy consumption increase, requiring a slower transformative energy scenario.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Renewable energy usage preference_qna_009
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does energy consumption impact energy accessibility, renewable energy penetration, and energy intensity?
nodes.answer: Energy consumption patterns influence energy accessibility, renewable energy penetration, and energy intensity, with higher energy consumption potentially leading to better renewable energy uptake and energy accessibility in certain scenarios.
